FIXED AND PROVEN. Change 2618: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2618 -- LLM-Review +1, plan review PASS with 0 blocking.

WORKFLOW_DISPATCH PROOF (run 33855430270, ref bug-860b-macos-git-probe, job 100967566130):
  sweep (macos, full suite) = SUCCESS
  before (main 6b034b9f8224): 19243 passed, 72 skipped, 422 warnings, 1 ERROR in 2687.89s
  after  (this fix):          19244 passed, 72 skipped, 460 warnings, 0 errors in 2707.41s
The +1 test is the new regression test. Verified against the actual schedule-gated job rather than
inferred.

MY PREMISE IN THIS TICKET WAS WRONG AND THE IMPLEMENTER CHECKED RATHER THAN INHERITING IT. I wrote
that the blamed test 'provisions a real Node toolchain (npm ci plus an esbuild bundle) and is the
heaviest thing in the suite'. It does not. It drives a shell STUB npm ('mkdir -p node_modules; exit
0') under tmp_path and is one of the CHEAPEST tests in the file. I was right that the cause was
contention and wrong about the mechanism, and my wrong mechanism would have sent a fix at the test.

READING (a) SETTLED ON EVIDENCE, not elimination:
 - '<Popen: returncode: -9 ...>' in the traceback -- the child was ALIVE and killed by the timeout.
   Running, not wedged.
 - 400 [rebar-ci-timing] warnings in that same run (threshold 1.0s), topping out at
   'built_distributions fixture_setup elapsed=4.562s' on a DIFFERENT worker. Ordinary fixture setup
   on that runner reaches 91% OF THE PROBE'S FIXED 5s BOUND. The bound sits inside the runner's own
   latency distribution.
So the defect is THE BOUND, not the test: one fixed-timeout sample of a read-only, idempotent probe
taken ~19,000 times, three xdist workers deep, across a 45-minute run.

READING (b) RULED OUT AT MECHANISM LEVEL rather than by assertion: there is no real npm/esbuild child
to leak; 'git rev-parse HEAD' reads .git/HEAD and refs and takes NO LOCK, so no leaked handle can
serialize against it; a patched clock is impossible because CPython binds 'from time import monotonic
as _time' in subprocess; and a leaked PATH was ruled out EXPERIMENTALLY -- monkeypatch is
function-scoped and non-autouse, so it finalizes before the autouse guard's post-yield.

THE FIX, and one design choice worth preserving: _run_git_probe re-samples a timed-out attempt up to
GIT_PROBE_ATTEMPTS = 3, with THE FINAL ATTEMPT OUTSIDE THE RETRY LOOP so a persistent TimeoutExpired
propagates unconditionally -- 'loudness is structural, not a conditional a later edit could invert'.
And no sleep between attempts: the elapsed per-attempt timeout IS the backoff, and sleeping would
re-introduce the patched-time.sleep hazard that _stable_subprocess_time exists to defend against.

AC4 HONOURED: the e2e test is untouched -- not skipped, not marked, not excluded. The fix is in the
probe, which is where the defect actually was.

AC3 verified by mutation: making head/porcelain swallow TimeoutExpired FAILS 3 tests, and
test_head_detects_a_commit / test_guard_fails_a_test_that_commits still detect a real HEAD move. The
guard is not weakened.

Defect-seeded RED in 25 seconds rather than a 45-minute run:
  subprocess.TimeoutExpired: Command '[git, -C, .../repo, rev-parse, HEAD]' timed out after 0.484s
  FAILED test_a_transient_probe_stall_is_re_sampled_rather_than_reported
GREEN with the fix: 23 passed.

Gates: make lint exit 0; make typecheck clean (755 files); the three pytest-only gates 54 passed (run
after git add); tests/unit + tests/e2e 15391 passed. No new mechanism.

Verified -1 comes SOLELY from scanner-integration (90c7, another session). Not closing until that
clears and 2618 merges.
